Then proceed with the first pull.

evals.expected_output: Should be idempotent apart from the log: no new Meetings/ files created, no existing Meetings/ files modified, no items added to the current week file. Should advance Sources/<channel>.md last_scan_ts to current time. Should append exactly one Logs/YYYY-MM.md entry with op `pull` recording 0 new threads and a complete sweep. evals.expected_output: Should look up slack_thread_ts in existing Meetings/*.md frontmatter, find the match, fetch only replies after slack_last_reply_ts, append them to ## Discussion with chronological date/author subheadings in user's local timezone, update slack_last_reply_ts in frontmatter, and run extraction on the appended content only. Should NOT rewrite ## Notes or any other existing content. Should NOT create a new Meetings note for the same thread_ts.
evals.issue_tested: Thread evolution - existing threads with new replies append cleanly without overwriting

A bulk reply (e.g. 'add 1; 2 as P2 under X; skip') applies edits correctly and regenerates frontmatter only if a top-level item was added.

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (context-channel containing only unrelated banter and logistics)
evals.expected_output: Should classify all units as noise and drop them silently - zero writes to any worklog item or note, no approval-batch entries. The summary reports them as dropped (count only).

evals.expected_output: Should be idempotent: ts > last_scan_ts yields no new units, so no auto-folds, no approval batch, no writes. last_scan_ts advances to current time. Summary reports 0 scanned/0 folded/0 surfaced/0 dropped for that channel.

evals.issue_tested: DM high-confidence match goes to approval batch, not auto-fold

evals.expected_output: On approval, the folded sub-item is a genericized, workstream-level summary (no verbatim 1:1 quote, no personal detail beyond the item's need), dated with the result's message_ts, wiki-linked, with the result's permalink for provenance.
evals.issue_tested: Approved DM items fold as genericized summaries with provenance

evals.expected_output: Should hit the volume guardrail up front: stop and tell the user the count and window, ask whether to proceed / narrow / skip. No silent truncation.
evals.issue_tested: DM-sweep volume guardrail at max_results - no silent truncation

evals.prompt: /worklog rollup
evals.expected_output: Should copy a Slack-mrkdwn version to the clipboard via pbcopy with no [[wiki-link]] syntax, AND write References/YYYY-WNN Rollup.md with type: reference, subtype: rollup, period, and source frontmatter. The same include/filter content rules apply to both renderings: no performance commentary, no 1:1 specifics, no candidate names in either. Should append one Logs/ entry with op `rollup`.

evals.prompt: /worklog share
evals.expected_output: Should copy a brief priority-grouped status blurb to the clipboard and write NO vault file. Filing a share is explicitly out of scope; 52 of these a year would be noise in References/. Should append no Logs/ entry.
evals.issue_tested: Not every output is worth filing - share and search stay ephemeral

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Nadia Okafor.md" (vault git state clean; note has ## Role (HR system, confirmed <today>), ## 1:1 Doc, dozens of dated ## entries, and one of those dated entries contains a nested ### Current Status subsection)
evals.expected_output: ## Role (HR system, confirmed <today>) and ## 1:1 Doc must come out byte-identical, at their original heading level and order, because they state what is true now, not because their headings lack a date - the same pattern as any dated-provenance heading such as ## Role (HR system, confirmed ...), which is current state precisely because it carries a confirmed-date stamp. A protection test keyed to 'heading has no date' would wrongly treat ## Role as foldable. The nested ### Current Status subsection must NOT get that same protection: because it sits beneath a dated entry, it is part of that entry and travels with it into ## Recent or ## History whole, rather than being promoted out as an independent current-state section.
evals.issue_tested: Current-state protection turns on what a section is for, not on whether its heading carries a date, and only applies to top-level sections - a current-state section nested inside a dated entry is not independently protected

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Ines Duarte.md" (1536 lines, never compacted; roughly 60 unique [[wiki-link]] targets across its dated entries; most of its dated entries currently sit inside the WORKLOG_COMPACT_KEEP_DAYS window)
evals.expected_output: Should capture canonical link targets before and after by materializing the proposal to a temp file and running the identical stripped-alias grep pipeline on both, not comparing by eye; any target present before and absent after must be named and explicitly confirmed before writing, never written-then-warned. Because most of this note's bulk currently falls inside the keep window and moves to ## Recent unchanged rather than folding, the pass is likely to leave the note still over WORKLOG_COMPACT_LINES; if so, the summary and log entry must state that explicitly with before/after line counts and the threshold and recommend a shorter WORKLOG_COMPACT_KEEP_DAYS - compacted: still updates to today, recording that a pass happened, not that the note is now small. The same materialized proposal must also be checked with the heading comparison: every heading that would vanish must be named as the bullet it folded into, since unlike a dropped link there is no confirmation path for an unexplained missing heading. The line-count drop must also reconcile against what was folded - if the note shrank by more than the sum of the folded sections' pre-fold line counts, that is a failed compaction regardless of whether the result lands under WORKLOG_COMPACT_LINES, and compacted: must not be reported as done.
evals.issue_tested: Link preservation is a hard gate on a materialized proposal, not a warning; and a partial fold on an oversized note must report its shortfall rather than claim success

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Nadia Okafor.md" (frontmatter says team: Northwind Platform and summary: "Director, Platform Ops"; the ## Role section records that Platform Ops was merged into Core Infrastructure and Northwind Platform renamed Core Infrastructure)
evals.expected_output: Should report both contradictions - team: versus the rename, and the existing summary: versus the merger - and NOT auto-fix either, even though the body is clearly newer and more complete. The user decides. A correct run still produces its own outputs (compacted: today, the History fold) but leaves team: and the stale summary: untouched pending the user's call; silently rewriting either field, or silently replacing the stale summary with a corrected one, is a failure - the deliverable is the report, not the fix.
evals.issue_tested: Contradiction detection reports and never auto-fixes, and that rule extends to a self-contradicting existing summary:, not just a frontmatter/body mismatch

evals.prompt: /worklog compact (no argument; the scanner's oversized_notes returns five candidates: People/Nadia Okafor.md (347 lines), People/Theo Kask.md (346), People/Ines Duarte.md (344), People/Sofia Brandt.md (334), People/Kenji Watanabe.md (325))
evals.expected_output: Should run the scanner, read oversized_notes, and offer the five candidates one at a time with explicit options, largest first - Nadia Okafor.md first, Kenji Watanabe.md last. Must not present all five as a single free-text checklist and must not move to a second note without a per-note decision on the one before it. A reply that tries to cover multiple notes at once is not a valid response to a one-at-a-time offer.
evals.issue_tested: No-argument compact offers oversized candidates one at a time in size order, not as a batch checklist

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Theo Kask.md" - run once when the vault has uncommitted changes, and once when the vault directory is not a git repository at all
evals.expected_output: Both cases must end in a refusal to write the fold, but they are not the same refusal. Dirty case: git status --porcelain prints output, so offer to run /worklog sync; afterward, re-run the check rather than assuming the sync cleaned everything, since sync's git add list is an explicit allowlist that can leave files unstaged; if the user declines or the re-check still reports dirty, name the outstanding files and stop without compacting. Not-a-repo case: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails, there is no undo available at all, and the correct response is an unconditional refusal - not a dirty-state warning, not an offer to sync, and not a proceed-anyway option.
evals.issue_tested: The git-clean precondition is a refusal, not a warning, and 'not a repo at all' is a distinct refusal path from 'dirty' - neither is satisfied by an unverified sync

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Sofia Brandt.md" (already has compacted: 2026-06-01 and a populated ## History whose newest bullet covers an Apr 2026 theme; several ## Recent entries from around that same June compaction have since aged past WORKLOG_COMPACT_KEEP_DAYS)
evals.expected_output: Existing ## History bullets must come out byte-identical - they are immutable once written, never re-folded or re-summarized even when a newly-aged entry continues the same theme. Entries that have aged past the keep window since June must move from ## Recent into ## History now, added as new bullets of their own rather than merged into or used to rewrite an existing bullet on that theme, since re-summarizing already-summarized text is exactly what immutability forbids. The retention window is measured from today, not from the 2026-06-01 compaction date. Frontmatter compacted: updates to today's date.
evals.issue_tested: Repeat compaction treats existing History as immutable and measures the retention window from today, not from the last compaction date - a themed continuation must still land as its own bullet, never merged into the old one

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Ines Duarte.md" with WORKLOG_COMPACT_KEEP_DAYS=1 (so the two Planning conversation entries from 80 days ago are past the window and become fold candidates). The first, "## <date> - 🔒 Planning conversation 10:00-10:05 AM (vault-only)", has a nested child "### 🔒 10:02 AM (ULTRA-CONFIDENTIAL)". The entry right after it, "## <date> - 🔒 Planning conversation 10:20-10:25 AM (vault-only)", carries the same two markers on its own heading but no ULTRA-CONFIDENTIAL child anywhere beneath it, and both entries cover the same planning theme.
evals.expected_output: The 10:00 entry has a handling-marker set of {🔒, vault-only, ULTRA-CONFIDENTIAL} - the union of its own heading's two markers and its nested child's one. The 10:20 entry has the same two markers on its own heading, and none of its nested children add a new token, so its union stays {🔒, vault-only}. Even though both cover the same planning theme and grouping same-theme entries into one bullet is normally preferred, these two entries must land in separate History bullets, because their marker sets are not identical: {🔒, vault-only} is a subset of {🔒, vault-only, ULTRA-CONFIDENTIAL}, and a subset relationship does not qualify for sharing. A wrong implementation that groups by theme first and checks markers second would merge them under the parent heading's own markers, {🔒, vault-only}, silently dropping the ULTRA-CONFIDENTIAL restriction and laundering the child's restricted content into a less-restricted bullet - the exact disclosure risk the union rule exists to prevent.
evals.issue_tested: A handling-marker set is the union of an entry's own heading markers and every nested child's markers, and only identical sets may share a History bullet - a same-theme, subset-marker entry must still split into its own bullet rather than let the child's tighter restriction get silently lost

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Kenji Watanabe.md" ([[Chris Moreau|Chris]] appears exactly once in the whole note, as a 360-feedback backup reviewer inside the old "## <date> - Active Workstreams" section, which is old enough today to be a fold candidate). The model proposes History bullet set A, compressing that 360-feedback line without keeping the Chris Moreau mention, and the user approves set A. Materializing set A and running the link-gate pipeline then reports [[Chris Moreau]] as a target that would be lost. The model revises to bullet set B, keeping a Chris Moreau reference, and B compares clean.
evals.expected_output: The approval given for set A does not carry over to set B. Because the link gate forced a revision, the model must show B's History bullets themselves - the actual bullet text, not a paraphrase or a change-note like 'kept the Chris Moreau mention' - and wait for a fresh approval before writing, even though B compares clean and the user already approved once. Writing B on the strength of the approval given for A is exactly the failure the revise-and-reapprove loop exists to prevent. What is shown for approval, both times, must also exclude the entries moving to ## Recent: those move unchanged, so pasting them adds nothing for the user to approve and is not part of what this gate requires.
evals.issue_tested: Approval does not carry across a link-gate revision - a revised proposal needs its own approval even when it compares clean - and what is shown for approval must be the actual History bullets, never a summary of them, and never padded with unchanged ## Recent content

evals.prompt: /worklog compact "People/Theo Kask.md" - the vault has never been initialized as a git repository
evals.expected_output: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails, so there is no undo available at all for a lossy fold. The correct response is an unconditional refusal: no dirty-vault language (no 'uncommitted', no 'git status', no mention of syncing), no offer to run /worklog sync, and no proceed-anyway option. The model should tell the user the vault is not under git version control, that there is no undo, and stop without writing anything.
evals.issue_tested: The not-a-repo refusal path is distinct from the dirty-vault refusal path and must not degrade into it - this covers the not-a-repo half of the git-clean precondition that case 36 leaves untested

evals.prompt:
quick note from today's migration sync:
- Theo confirmed the rollback rehearsal is scheduled for Friday

add to worklog
evals.expected_output: Should fold this as a dated sub-item under the existing Platform Migration cutover item (do not create a new top-level item). What this case actually grades: the rehearsal detail must be genuinely present in the current week file when the model reports success. A run that claims the note was added, updated, or logged without that text landing in Worklogs/<week>.md is the false-success failure from issue #19 - the fix is a mandatory re-read-and-confirm step before reporting success, not more self-reporting language. If the write genuinely fails, the model must say so explicitly (retry once, then report failure) rather than claim success.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #19 - model (measured on Haiku) reports confident success on natural-language ingest without writing the extracted fact to the week file; tests that success is only reported after a verified re-read confirms the item actually landed, not asserted from the write attempt alone.

evals.prompt: /worklog add P1 finish the vendor security questionnaire under Platform Migration
evals.expected_output: Item lands under Platform Migration exactly as a normal /worklog add would. add routes to Haiku. evals.prompt: /worklog rollover
evals.expected_output: Should apply the retention rule from references/threads.md: carry each not-Done item forward with only its newest WORKLOG_WEEK_KEEP_SUBS dated sub-items plus any open action regardless of age, write the displaced sub-items verbatim into a Threads/<slug>.md note BEFORE pruning the week file, append a 'Full history: [[Threads/<slug>]]' pointer, and park the item whose newest dated sub-item is outside WORKLOG_WEEK_DORMANT_DAYS. Nothing may be lost: every pre-rollover sub-item line must still exist in the week file, Backlog.md or a Thread note.

evals.expected_output: The DM sweep must fan out: pass several narrow queries on stdin to slack-search-dms (names from the current week file and vault), not run it once with no queries. The group DM candidate reaches the end-of-pull approval batch and is not auto-folded.
evals.issue_tested: DM sweep missed a same-day group DM because it ran one relevance-ranked query; fan-out or a chronological listing is required

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (Sources/_dms.md enabled; the DM candidate is about a topic that already has a parked Backlog entry and a Thread; the reply approves the recommended option)
